Listed Futures Market Basics

A listed futures contract is a standardised exchange-traded product with a defined unit, quote, minimum price increment, expiry/settlement and exchange rulebook. A platform symbol may show one expiry or a vendor-mapped continuous series; these are not interchangeable.

Continuous Contract Mapping

A continuous futures symbol links multiple expiring listed contracts into a vendor/platform series. Roll date, adjustment and splice can alter the visible price history; the continuous series is useful for context but is not itself an executable expiry contract.

Futures Margin & Position Risk

Margin is collateral required by an FCM/broker and clearing venue; it is not the same as planned loss at a structural stop. Stop risk depends on ticks, tick value, contract count and transaction costs, with gaps/slippage potentially increasing loss.

Futures Volume, Open Interest & COT

Exchange volume counts traded contracts in an interval; open interest counts outstanding open contracts at a reporting time; CFTC COT classifies aggregate positions at a report cadence. They are distinct measures and cannot replace each other or order-book depth.

Evidence and source standards

SOURCED means a named source must support the exact claim. CONVENTION identifies community practice or editorial synthesis. NO DATA means independently audited public performance evidence was not located in the reviewed material. HYPOTHESIS is a testable interpretation. TESTED is reserved for a reproducible test with dataset, dates, costs, rules, sample size and out-of-sample results.

The 39-page playbook discloses limitations in its source review: some details were taken from search excerpts, and ICT original videos plus Reddit/Discord were not exhaustively reviewed. A channel/playlist or topic search is discovery, not a verified one-to-one video citation. Contract, tick, margin, session, roll and event values must be rechecked from current primary sources.
